site.name: Block Builder
site.headline: Minecraft plugins, shown in action.
site.tagline: Two Paper plugins: a crash-safe bounty economy and an SMP built on borrowed time. Watch them run, then read how they work.
site.about: Block Builder is a solo plugin studio for Minecraft servers. I build Paper-first game systems — bounty economies, time-based SMPs, hardened GUIs — with crash-safe storage, validated configs and tests behind the money paths. If a player can break it at 3am, the ledger still has to balance.

projects.title: BountySystem
projects.tagline: Escrowed player bounties with a full GUI — post a bounty, hunt the target, claim the reward.
projects.body:
BountySystem turns any server into a bounty economy. Players escrow real value — diamonds from a chest vault or server money through Vault — place a bounty on an online player's head, and the killer claims it. Every coin moves through a crash-safe SQLite ledger, so a restart mid-payout never eats a diamond.

## Features

- **Seven-menu GUI** — board, browse, target detail, target picker, reward amount, confirm, and my bounties — all reachable with `/bounty`.
- **Physical escrow** — diamonds held in a chest vault, or Vault economy. What is promised is what gets paid.
- **Crash-safe ledger** — every escrow, refund and payout is an audited SQLite WAL transaction. Stuck entries can be resolved by hand.
- **Hardened menus** — identity-checked InventoryHolders, every interaction cancelled, sessions die on close or quit. The GUI never moves money itself.
- **Config that refuses to break** — the whole file is validated on load and on `/bounty reload`; an invalid edit leaves the last good config running.

## Commands

| Command | What it does | Permission |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/bounty` | Opens the bounty board GUI | `bounty.use` |
| `/bounty list` | Lists every active bounty with its id | `bounty.use` |
| `/bounty place <player> <amount>` | Escrows and places a bounty on an online player | `bounty.use` |
| `/bounty cancel <id>` | Cancels one of your bounties — an 8-character id prefix works | `bounty.use` |
| `/bounty reload` | Validates and applies a changed config | `bounty.admin` |
| `/bounty admin ledger` | Lists open ledger entries needing review | `bounty.admin` |
| `/bounty admin bounties` | Every bounty record ever stored, with status | `bounty.admin` |
| `/bounty admin resolve <id> refund\|reject` | Unsticks a ledger entry: refund pays now, reject closes it | `bounty.admin` |

Every subcommand has tab completion — online targets for `place`, your own ids for `cancel`, and the full `admin` tree for staff.

## Install

Build with `gradlew build`, take `build/libs/BountySystem-0.1.0.jar` into your `plugins/` folder, restart. First run creates `plugins/BountySystem/bounties.db` and the default config. v0.1.0 is available on GitHub Releases; the source is in the repo.

Paper 26.3 · Java 25 · 58 tests

projects.title: LifeClock
projects.tagline: An SMP where every player lives on borrowed time — the clock drains while you play, PvP costs you two hours, and only a sacrifice brings you back.
projects.body:
LifeClock is a time-economy SMP for Paper. Every player starts with **24 hours** on a sidebar clock that drains one second per second while they are online. At zero they become a **Ghost** in spectator mode; the only way back is a teammate willing to spend their own time.

## What happens

- **The clock drains while online** — one second per second, shown in a sidebar HUD titled TIME. Numbers turn green above 10 hours, yellow from 5–10, red below 5, and flash red/white under 1 hour.
- **PvP costs two hours** — a victim loses 2 hours and drops a Time Clock at the death spot. Anyone can pick it up and right-click it for +2h.
- **Zero means Ghost** — at zero seconds the player becomes a Ghost in spectator mode. Their time and Ghost state survive restarts and reconnects.
- **Revive Totem** — crafted shapeless from a totem, golden apple, diamond and blaze rod. Right-clicking one opens the **54-slot ghost menu** (player heads plus a compass search slot); the revive costs the reviver **5 hours** of their own clock and gives the revived player **2 hours**.
- **Withdraw time** — `/withdraw` converts your own clock into tradeable Time Clock items, either from presets or a custom amount. It refuses to empty your clock.
- **Persistence** — state lives in `times.yml`, saved on changes, every minute and on shutdown.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/lifeclock add <player> <time>` | Adds time to a player’s clock |
| `/lifeclock remove <player> <time>` | Removes time from a player’s clock |
| `/lifeclock set <player> <time>` | Sets the clock directly |
| `/lifeclock check <player>` | Shows a player’s remaining time |
| `/lifeclock revive <player>` | Revives a Ghost |
| `/withdraw <time>` | Withdraws time into a Time Clock item — `/withdraw` alone opens the preset menu |

`/lifeclock` requires `lifeclock.admin` (op by default); `/withdraw` is for every player. Durations accept `45s`, `90m`, `2h`, `1d` or plain seconds.

## Install

Built against **Paper 1.21.11** and **Java 21**. Build with `mvn package`, drop the jar into `plugins/`, and restart. The source is public at [LifeClock-Plugin](https://github.com/vuranimation767-byte/LifeClock-Plugin).
